articleTitle: Wide Bandgap Power to Electrify Our World for a Sustainable Future
abstract: In this article we look at how we can most efficiently “Electrify our World” to reduce emissions and meet net-zero goals by using wide bandgap semiconductors. Based on third party verified life-cycle analysis and sustainability reporting, this article will show how GaN and SiC enable not only CO2 reductions through in-use efficiency but can also support reduced emissions through creation (making the chip) and dematerialization (reducing system size and materials used). We will also illustrate how these technologies not only optimize efficiency but can support increased uptake of electrification thanks to the resulting benefits.

articleTitle: Advances in SiC Technologies Address High-Voltage Electrification Design Challenges
abstract: The move to a more-electrified society that is critical for global environmental sustainability is a key driver behind the rapid growth in deployment of silicon carbide (SiC) semiconductors. Capable of operating at higher voltages than their silicon counterparts, SiC devices in general offer superior efficiency, faster switching speeds and more robust operation—particularly at high temperatures. Now, devices at the 3.3 kV rating and above are becoming particularly important in higher-power applications. This article looks at the latest developments in GeneSiC technology, and the benefits those bring to new and emerging high-voltage applications, and how such devices can be deployed.

articleTitle: High Current Density Power Modules Mitigate the Environmental Impact of Power-Intensive GenAI
abstract: Datacenters consume a stunning amount of energy to power and cool generative artificial intelligence (genAI), compute and infrastructure hardware. The training of genAI artificial neural network models typically consumes months of time, with thousands of multi-billion transistor processors, high-bandwidth semiconductor and magnetic memories, and optical network processors operating perpetually <xref ref-type="bibr" rid="ref1" xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[1]</xref>, <xref ref-type="bibr" rid="ref2" xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[2]</xref>. The New York Times has reported that “In a middle-ground scenario, by 2027 AI servers could use between 85 to 134 terawatt hours (TWh) annually <xref ref-type="bibr" rid="ref3" xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[3]</xref>.” GenAI model training presents a daunting and pressing power consumption challenge which is misaligned with societal net zero and greenhouse gas reduction objectives.

articleTitle: 1.2 kV/400 A SiC Source Turn-Off MOSFET Intelligent Power Module
abstract: Excellent switching performances and higher levels of integration are two critical topics for intelligent power modules (IPM). This article proposes a novel and cost effective 1.2 kV/400 A SiC half-bridge power module based on the Source Turn-off (STO) MOSFET. STO MOSFET is a driver integrated MOSFET architecture that can achieve ultra-fast turn-on and turn-off operations beyond the traditional voltage source gate driver approach. A built-in current and temperature monitoring features are also integrated. The IPM integrates discrete SiC devices, direct bond copper (DBC) base plate, STO gate driver, auxiliary power supply, current monitor, temperature monitor, and decoupling caps, making it plug-and-play ready.

articleTitle: Plenary Speakers Chart New Path for Power Technologies at APEC 2024
abstract: This year, the 39th global applied power electronics event, the IEEE Applied Power Electronics Conference and Exposition (APEC) 2024 was held in Long Beach, CA, USA, from 25–29 February. Breaking all previous records, APEC 2024 registered over 6000 attendees from around the world, who convened in Long Beach Convention Center to discuss and showcase latest advances in power semiconductors, electronic components, modules, packaging, test and measurement equipments, modeling and simulation tools, and much more. It was well represented by both academia and industry. While the exhibit floor was filled with over 300 booths, with the exhibitors enthusiastically displaying their latest products and services that deliver solutions to existing and emerging problems. The conference was cosponsored by the IEEE Power Electronics Society (PELS), Power Sources Manufacturers Association (PSMA), and the IEEE Industry Applications Society (IAS).

articleTitle: Building the Electric Power Grid One Unit at a Time
abstract: As the world experiences an electrical revolution at a historic scale, equally historic innovations are essential to meet the changing demands of the electric grid. Beginning with light bulbs and moving forward through motor drives—all the way to today’s renewable energy sources and the electrification of load sectors—global advances in electrical technology now rely on power electronics (PE). It is a key technology for power conditioning and grid integration of distributed energy resources and for delivering power over long distances mainly from offshore wind and utility-scale solar farms. The technology is vital for management and conversion of energy for end-use applications such as megawatt-scale charging infrastructure and industrial processes and equipment.

articleTitle: ESD Protection for Power Electronic ICs and Discrete Devices
abstract: Today’s power electronics systems are providing amazing advancements in power density, features and functionality. Industrial, lighting, medical, communications and other critical systems perform sophisticated functions—controlling, monitoring and reporting data. Expected to maintain long and continuous operation, often in harsh environments, these systems are subject to increasingly stringent safety and warranty regulations. Compounding this challenge for electronic design engineers, state-of-the-art systems typically employ modern semiconductors often vulnerable to electrostatic discharge (ESD) and other transient events. This article addresses the design and regulatory challenges that come with protecting the newest generation of power electronics systems against the problem of ESD causing safety issues during manufacturing and product failures down the line. It presents a simple protection approach: replacing standard rectifiers used in the system’s power converter with automotive-qualified, ESD-capable rectifiers.

articleTitle: Development of Power Electronics Systems in Industrial and Automotive Environments
abstract: The power electronics plays a significant role in modern applications like home appliances, consumer electronics, industry, automotive, renewables, etc. This article will provide an overview, definitions, and address typical challenges in a development process of low-voltage power converters. Independent of converter size, complexity and power level, the development process is more or less similar. This is tutorial-like article aimed to help students, engineers or academic staff who are starting on a path of hardware (HW) development. Thus, saving learning time (and costs) of everyone involved in the process. It is based on author’s experience and tutorials that were delivered at international symposiums on power electronics. Typically, academic staff and researchers are focused roughly on the first 20% of the total work needed to develop a product. But, 80% of the remaining work to finalize a product and bring it to the market is challenging. Hence, the goal here is to get a basic understanding of the development process and better prepare newcomers to the world of power electronics HW development.

articleTitle: Energy Efficiency is Not Enough!
abstract: In its latest report, the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) concludes that any further increase of global temperatures aggravates climate-related risks like species losses, extreme heat and humidity with significant consequences for human health, or negative impacts on food production and water availability; the projected negative outcomes escalate with higher temperature increases <xref ref-type="bibr" rid="ref1" xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[1]</xref>. Therefore, worldwide efforts and international policymaking (i.e., The Paris Agreement from 2015) aim at limiting global warming by the end of the 21st century to well below +2°C above pre-industrial levels, preferably to not more than +1.5°C.

articleTitle: Alternative Way to Develop Small-Signal Models of Power Converters
abstract: The small-signal model of a switch-mode power converter is a useful tool in understanding its dynamic behavior and designing a proper compensator. In the power electronics community, people derive small-signal models almost always by perturbation and then extracting the small ac components manually from the whole system equations. This process is not systematic and potentially error prone. This article presents an alternative process to develop small-signal models based on a well-established systematic method that has been used in control system analysis and design for a long period. With this math-centric approach, one just applies standard math operation to linearize a nonlinear system described by its state-space equation, and then uses a well-known formula to derive the transfer functions of the linearized system. This is a precisely defined and systematic process with the advantage of deriving all the transfer functions with a minimum effort.

articleTitle: Sustainability of Power Electronics and Batteries: A Circular Economy Approach
abstract: Power electronics and battery energy storage are the key enabling technologies for high-efficiency energy conversions to realize green transition. With an increasing demand for electrification, renewable energy integration, and energy saving, more and more power electronics and batteries are being utilized. Consequently, their impact on the environment becomes of great concern, as they are responsible for a considerable amount of material usage including critical raw material during production and e-waste generation after the end-of-life. Going forward, the development of power electronics and batteries needs to change from the traditional linear economy “take-make-waste” to a circular economy, where the concept of reuse, remanufacturing, and recycling needs to be considered as part of the product life cycle. In this article, challenges and potential solutions to enhance the sustainability of power electronics and batteries through the concept of circular economy will be addressed both from the design and end-of-life management perspectives. Existing design tools and their application in the power electronic industry will also be discussed as well as future demand.

articleTitle: Learning-by-Doing: Design and Implementation of a Solar Array Simulator With a SYNDEM Smart Grid Research and Educational Kit
abstract: Topics in control and power electronics play a pivotal role in the transition of power systems from centralized generation to distributed generation, the electrification of transportation, and the improvement of the lives of billions in developing countries. Numerous active sources, such as wind farms, solar farms, distributed energy resources, electric vehicles, energy storage systems, and flexible loads, are being integrated into power systems through power electronic converters <xref ref-type="bibr" rid="ref1" xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[1]</xref>. These demand for skilled power electronics and control engineers with a robust foundation in theoretical knowledge, complemented with extensive practical experiences, to effectively navigate emerging and rapidly evolving technologies in the realm of renewable energy. Therefore, enhancing learning effectiveness in these fields is critical for students to bridge the gap between theoretical knowledge and industrial settings. The concept of learning-by-doing emerged in recent decades is a compelling approach that can significantly improve engineering education, particularly, in the context of power electronics and control. It is a dynamic method in which students investigate real-world problems and challenges, fostering not only a deeper understanding of the subject matter but also increasing their engagement levels and critical thinking <xref ref-type="bibr" rid="ref2" xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[2]</xref>. Additional advantages include fostering active, self-motivated student engagement in the learning process and empowering them to address doubts independently. This approach may lead to a more effective learning experience than relying solely on a teacher, as students gain heightened awareness of specific challenges through firsthand experiences in solving real-world problems and make new contributions in the field <xref ref-type="bibr" rid="ref3" xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[3]</xref>.

articleTitle: Proposing a Duty Cycle Based Repetitive Drain Overvoltage Specification for GaN HEMTs
abstract: Transient voltage overshoot is a common phenomenon in wide bandgap (WBG) power semiconductors due to high frequency and fast switching applications. An application driven repetitive transient off-state overvoltage datasheet specification is desired for design engineers. In this work, a 1% duty-cycle-based overvoltage specification is proposed by estimating the total lifetime before the dynamic <inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{DS}(\text { on) }}$ </tex-math></inline-formula> shift exceeds 20% increase to its initial value under 120% of <inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{DS}, \text { Max }}$ </tex-math></inline-formula> continuous bias and <inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">${75}^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ </tex-math></inline-formula> junction temperature. This 1% duty cycle suggests that GaN devices can withstand a 1% duration of each switching period repetitively over 25 years of continuous switching.

articleTitle: IEEE Joint IAS/PELS/IES German Chapter Visits Multiple Facilities
abstract: The IEEE Joint Industry Applications Society (IAS)/Power Electronics Society (PELS)/Industrial Electronics Society (IES) German Chapter recently organized a two-day trip for visiting multiple facilities involved in the field of power electronics.

articleTitle: On a Road to Net Zero Emissions [From the Editor]
abstract: <fig orientation="portrait" position="float" xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"> <graphic orientation="portrait" position="float" xlink:href="bindr-3356261.tif"/> </fig> Today, sustainability is the buzz word and countries around the world are working together to address a common challenge, the climate change. The latest report by the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change indicates that any further increase of global temperatures would have adverse impact on human health, environment, agriculture, water availability, and multitude of other Earth related problems. Therefore, worldwide efforts are underway, including international protocols and agreements (e.g., The Paris Agreement of 2015), aiming to limit global warming by the end of the 21st century to well below +2°C, preferably to +1.5°C.

articleTitle: Technical University of Munich Announces Passing of Prof. Dierk F. Schroeder [In Memoriam]
abstract: With immense sadness, Technical University of Munich (TUM), Germany, announced the passing of Prof. Dr.-Ing. Dr. h.c. Dierk F. Schroeder on 23 March 2024 in Munich, Germany. He was a Professor of Power Electronics and Electrical Drives (later: Mechatronics) at the TUM from 1983 until 2008. Prof. Schroeder was born on 7 January 1941 in Stendal, Germany.

articleTitle: IEEE PELS Kolkata Section Chapter Organizes DL Presentation
abstract: On 17 November 2023, the IEEE Power Electronics Society (PELS) Kolkata Section Chapter organized a Distinguished Lecturer (DL) presentation at the School of Electrical Engineering at Kalinga Institute of Industrial Technology, Bhubaneswar, Odisha, India. The Chapter was glad to host PELS DL Dr. Sanjib Kumar Panda and listen to his lecture on “A Futuristic Medium-Voltage Grid-Connected Multi-Port Public Electric-Vehicle Ultra-Fast Charging-Station with G2V and V2G Capability.”

articleTitle: Advances in Packaging Crucial to Powering Next Generation Processors [From the Editor]
abstract: <fig orientation="portrait" position="float" xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"> <graphic orientation="portrait" position="float" xlink:href="bindr-3397154.tif"/> </fig>Over the years, with advances in semiconductor processing, microprocessors have become more powerful and consume much more power as voltages dropped. Concurrently, power supplies designed to power these devices got more sophisticated, delivering more power at high efficiency from a smaller package with faster transient response and minimal noise and EMI. Aside from improvements in topology, circuit design, including magnetics, advances in packaging played a crucial role in building power supplies for next generation processors. Today, powerful artificial intelligence (AI) processors with billions of transistors on-chip, and offering tera floating point operations per second, are capable of handling more than 1000 A at voltages below 1 V. Powering these new generation processors requires power supplies that can be placed as close as possible to the processor to minimize parasitics while capable of handling thermal challenges.

articleTitle: IEEE PELS Swiss Chapter Hosts Workshop on Green Hydrogen
abstract: On 8 January 2024, the IEEE Industry Applications Society (IAS)/Power Electronics Society (PELS) Singapore Joint Chapter, Centre for System Intelligence and Efficiency, and School of Electrical Engineering at Nanyang Technological University (NTU) in Singapore hosted a technical seminar at NTU that focused on the development trends and challenges in application and reliability of power semiconductor devices (<xref ref-type="fig" rid="fig1" xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Figure 1</xref>).

articleTitle: IEEE PES/IAS/PELS Dallas Joint Chapter Hosts Talk on Hyper-Scale Datacenters
abstract: On 20 March, the IEEE Power and Energy Society (PES)/Industry Applications Society (IAS)/Power Electronics Society (PELS) Dallas Joint Chapter hosted a talk that focused on hyper-scale datacenters at the Parrish-Hare Electrical Supply, Irving, TX, USA. The keynote speaker was Jonathan Wheelis, who is a consulting application engineer with Schneider Electric. His presentation focused on hyper-scale datacenters and provided valuable insights into the key features, power system architecture, and benefits of hyper-scale datacenters (<xref ref-type="fig" rid="fig1" xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Figure 1</xref>). This emphasized their critical role in the power and engineering industries. Additionally, he highlighted the scalability, efficiency, and reliability advantages of hyper-scale datacenters by discussing lessons from Schneider Electric’s solutions for the entire powertrain design, which includes equipment from the medium voltage switchgear down to the PDU/PowerBus level.

articleTitle: A New Event: IEEE PELS Student Symposium on Power Electronics—Asia [Students and Young Professionals Rendezvous]
abstract: The second IEEE Power Electronics Society (PELS) Students Symposium on Power Electronics (SSPEL)—Asia 2024 was successfully held in Hangzhou, China, from 13 to 14 January 2024 with both in-person and virtual attendees. The event was organized through the joint efforts of the IEEE PELS Membership Committee—China (MCC), PELS Zhejiang/Jiangsu/Anhui Chapter, and PELS Zhejiang University Student Branch Chapter (SBC), with technical co-sponsorship of the China Power Supply Society (CPSS), as well as seven SBCs and the IEEE PELS Students and Young Professional (S&YP) Committee. The Symposium attracted 478 students and young professionals from seven countries, including, but not limited to, China, Singapore, and South Korea (<xref ref-type="fig" rid="fig1" xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Figure 1</xref>).

articleTitle: IEEE PELS TC 10 Organizes 3rd Edition of DMC
abstract: Last year, the IEEE PELS TC 10 organized the 3rd edition of the IEEE Design Methodologies Conference (DMC) at the Florida International University (FIU) in Miami, Florida, USA, from 24 to 26 September 2023. DMC aims at promoting new techniques and design methodologies in power electronics while identifying challenges and discussing the potential of new design and analysis paradigms in power electronics.

articleTitle: A Glance at the 2024 “Power Magnetics @ High Frequency” Workshop [PSMA Corner]
abstract: The field of power magnetics plays a crucial role in enabling advancements in electronic power converters. The ninth “Power Magnetics @ High Frequency” workshop returned to its inaugural site in Long Beach, CA, USA, on 24 February 2024, and brought together experts and enthusiasts to discuss the latest developments in magnetic materials, coil design, fabrication techniques, evaluation methods, and modeling tools (<xref ref-type="fig" rid="fig1" xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Figure 1</xref>). This review highlights the key insights and contributions from the workshop, focusing on the theme of designing optimal magnetics across applications and environments.

articleTitle: Vibrant Music City Energizes Fourteenth ECCE With Advances for Sustainability
abstract: Last year, the 14th IEEE Energy Conversion Congress & Expo (ECCE 2023), which was held in the exciting music city Nashville, TN, USA from 29 October to 2 November, set new records in attendance and paper presentations. Besides the usual technical program with over 1000 presentations, the 14th ECCE delivered many new features, such as offering both industry-driven and application-oriented technical sessions, an all-female keynote opening session, a historic milestone for IEEE Power Electronics Society (PELS), a major expansion in its exhibit hall programs and sponsorship opportunities, two-page late-breaking research papers in addition to their usual full-length papers, public outreach events and partnerships with local community organizations. Plus, subsidized daycare for attendee families.

articleTitle: PwrSoC’23 Focuses on Miniaturization of Power Conversion Solutions On-Chip, In-Package, and Module
abstract: From 27 to 29 September 2023, the 8th edition of the biennial International Workshop on Power Supply on Chip (PwrSoC) took place at Leibniz University in Hannover, Germany (<xref ref-type="fig" rid="fig1" xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Figure 1</xref>), sponsored by the IEEE Power Electronics Society (PELS) and the Power Sources Manufacturers Association (PSMA). General chair Bernhard Wicht and Technical Program chair Bruno Allard, organized and presided over a well-received workshop.

articleTitle: Silicon Power Growth Will Continue as WBG Power Technologies Increase [Expert View]
abstract: While wide bandgap (WBG) power devices are growing rapidly, Infineon expects that silicon (Si) power switching devices will continue to dominate the market for the remainder of the decade. Infineon has a unique position in the market by offering all three switching technologies: Si, silicon carbide (SiC), and gallium nitride (GaN). With this broad perspective, we see no threat from WBG devices reducing the total market size of Si power switching near term. Companies, like Infineon, will continue to invest in R&D and manufacturing to advance silicon power technology for those applications where the efficiency gains of WBG devices are not required and where cost and multi-source availability are paramount.

articleTitle: PELS SBC at NHCE and Bangalore Chapter Jointly Organize Multiple Events
abstract: IEEE Power Electronics Society’s (PELS) New Horizon College of Engineering (NHCE) Student Branch Chapter (SBC) at the Department of Electrical and Electronics Engineering, India and IEEE PELS Bangalore Chapter jointly organized the student technical event called “PRAUDYOGEEK 2.0” from 19 to 20 October 2022 for the benefit of B.E./B.Tech. students of NHCE and other external institutions (<xref ref-type="fig" rid="fig1" xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Figure 1</xref>). The aim behind the event was to help the participants get familiarized with basic electrical core concepts, as well as inspire constructive dialogue on trending topics in the technology field through a group discussion.

articleTitle: IEEE PELS Orange County Chapter Hosts Successful Debut Event
abstract: On 28 February, the IEEE Power Electronics Society (PELS) Orange County Chapter hosted its first presentation in collaboration with IEEE at the University of California, Irvine. The presentation had the topic “SMART Power Flow Controllers: A Necessity for Future Power Grids” and was given by Dr. Kalyan Sen (<xref ref-type="fig" rid="fig1" xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Figure 1</xref>). During the presentation, Dr. Sen explained how these controllers optimize existing transmission lines and ensure that future grids operate efficiently. A discussion between Dr. Sen and the over 20 attendees followed the presentation.

articleTitle: Keynote Lecture Presented at IEEE PELS Connecticut Chapter Kickoff Event
abstract: On 10 October 2023, the new IEEE Power Electronics Society (PELS) Connecticut Chapter hosted its inaugural event at the University of Connecticut (UConn), USA. The keynote lecture and reception featuring students’ power electronics demonstrations were attended by 45 engineers from academia and industry from around New England (<xref ref-type="fig" rid="fig1" xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Figure 1</xref>). The new PELS chapter collaborated with IEEE PELS and PES Chapters in Connecticut, Massachusetts, and New York for this event, which was sponsored by the UConn ECE Department and the Power Electronics & Drives Advanced Research Laboratory (PEARL).

articleTitle: Addressing the Global Energy Poverty Crisis [Empower a Billion Lives]
abstract: Welcome to a new quarterly column, entitled “Empower a Billion Lives,” a phrase that you may have already heard at IEEE events or from colleagues. I’ll take this inaugural column to introduce IEEE Power Electronics Society (PELS) community to EBL—as we like to call it—and the global problem of energy access, which we seek to address. If you will indulge me, I will take you through my own journey of getting involved with EBL and explain it all along the way.

articleTitle: Power Electronic Activities in Brazil: The Beginning [South American Power Electronics]
abstract: This column will try to disclose the power electronics (PE) activities in South American countries, namely Argentina, Brazil, Chisle, and Venezuela that interact with IEEE Power Electronics Society (PELS). It will also include activities in Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Uruguay. This first article, however, will focus only on Brazil’s PE history, which comprises developments based on three areas: industry, utility companies, and academia.

articleTitle: IEEE IES/IAS/PELS Gujarat Section Joint Chapter Organizes Expert Talk
abstract: On 7 February, the IEEE Industrial Electronics Society (IES)/Industry Applications Society (IAS)/Power Electronics Society (PELS) Gujarat Section Joint Chapter hosted an expert talk with the topic “Role of Digital Technology in Green Energy Transition” that was presented by Prof. Sri Niwas Singh (Indian Institute of Technology—Kanpur).

articleTitle: IEEE IES/PELS/IAS/PES Estonia Joint Chapter Collaborates With IEEE PELS Switzerland Chapter
abstract: On 6 March, the IEEE Industrial Electronics Society (IES)/Power Electronics Society (PELS)/Industry Applications Society (IAS)/Power and Energy Society (PES) Estonia Joint Chapter organized a lecture on “High-Power Medium-Voltage Solid-State Conversion” that was given by Prof. Drazen Dujic from the Swiss Federal Institute of Technology in Lausanne (EPFL), Switzerland, at the Tallinn University of Technology (TalTech), Estonia.

articleTitle: Newly Revived IEEE PELS Boston Chapter Hosts Meet & Greet and Women’s Day Events
abstract: This year on 22 February, the newly revived IEEE Power Electronics Society (PELS) Boston Chapter hosted its inaugural meet and greet even at the Northeastern University (NU), Boston, MA, USA. This hybrid event was attended by over 60 engineers from academia and industry around the greater Boston area (<xref ref-type="fig" rid="fig1" xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Figure 1</xref>).

articleTitle: Remembering the Exceptional Contributions of Prof. Ned Mohan [In Memoriam]
abstract: It is with great sadness that IEEE Power Electronics Society (PELS) announces the passing of Prof. Ned Mohan on 11 February 2024 in Minneapolis, MN at the age of 77. Prof. Mohan was born on 5 October 1946 in New Delhi, India. He received his undergraduate education from the Indian Institute of Technology Kharagpur, India in 1967. He received his Ph.D. degree from the University of Wisconsin, Madison, USA, in 1973. After a brief post-doctoral stint, he joined the University of Minnesota at the Twin Cities of Minneapolis-St. Paul in 1976. He spent his entire academic career spanning 48 years here. Since 1993, he was the Oscar A. Schott Professor of Power Electronics and Systems.

articleTitle: IEEE IAS/PELS Singapore Joint Chapter Hosts Seminar on Power Semiconductor Devices
abstract: On 8 January 2024, the IEEE Industry Applications Society (IAS)/Power Electronics Society (PELS) Singapore Joint Chapter, Centre for System Intelligence and Efficiency, and School of Electrical Engineering at Nanyang Technological University (NTU) in Singapore hosted a technical seminar at NTU that focused on the development trends and challenges in application and reliability of power semiconductor devices (<xref ref-type="fig" rid="fig1" xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Figure 1</xref>).

articleTitle: Powering Society’s Progress Together [President’s Message]
abstract: <fig orientation="portrait" position="float" xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"> <graphic orientation="portrait" position="float" xlink:href="lehma-3390328.tif"/> </fig>Exciting News! The IEEE Power Electronics Society (PELS) has just launched its revamped website at <uri xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">www.ieee-pels.org</uri>. After over a year of dedicated work, involving significant contributions from numerous volunteers on the publicity committee - Helen Cui, Rakesh Kumar, Dong Cao, Yuan Li, and Bright Tetteth - and the diligent effots of PELS staff members Mike Kelly and Jessica Uherek, we’re thrilled to unveil this updated platform. The countless hours invested in this project have certainly paid off, evident in the substantial improvements over the previous site, which I always admired. Our aim is to establish the PELS website as the premier destination for all things related to power electronics. This new iteration marks the initial stride towards achieving that goal, with ongoing plans to enhance its functionality in the future.

articleTitle: Not Your Grandpa’s Flyback [White Hot]
abstract: <fig orientation="portrait" position="float" xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"> <graphic orientation="portrait" position="float" xlink:href="white-3350272.tif"/> </fig> Reading recent conference papers, journal articles, and the trade press articles one would think that power electronics consisted only of dual active bridge (DAB) converters, various types of multi-level converters, and modular multi-level converters (MMC). These are all important to power electronics. DABs are very useful. They can be designed for a wide range of power, offer isolation, offer a wide range of possible conversion ratios. Their ability to process power equally well between two or more power ports makes them very useful to interface between dc power buses and batteries.

articleTitle: PELS Puzzlers Recreate Crossword Puzzles [Society News]
abstract: IEEE Power Electronics Society (PELS) Puzzlers is a recreational engineering community that solves brain-teasers and puzzles related to the fields of interest of the Society that includes the development and application of power electronic systems and technologies, which encompass the effective use of electronic components, the application of circuit theory and design techniques, and the development of analytical methods and tools for efficient electronic conversion, control, and conditioning of electric power to enable the sustainable use of energy.

articleTitle: IEEE PELS SBC at VIT, India Celebrate National Energy Conservation Day
abstract: To commemorate National Energy Conservation Day, the IEEE Power Electronics Society (PELS) Student Branch Chapter (SBC) at the Vellore Institute of Technology (VIT, Vellore) in India organized an awareness program that focused on energy conservation from 1 to 5 November 2023.

articleTitle: Power Technology Roadmap: Forecasting the Futur
abstract: <fig orientation="portrait" position="float" xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"> <graphic orientation="portrait" position="float" xlink:href="yawge-3352950.tif"/> </fig> In a world where the demand for electrical power is surging due to the proliferation of IoT edge devices, electric vehicles, and cloud computing, the Power Technology Roadmap (PTR) aims to assist the power electronics industry understand and anticipate the evolution of power conversion technology. The PTR, designed to offer a consolidated outlook of trends in power conversion technology, components, and applications for the next two to five years, recently resumed its webinar series, featuring presentations by industry experts and thought leaders. Let’s delve into the key insights shared in the recent PTR webinars.

articleTitle: Expediting Green Energy Transition [Expert View]
abstract: According to International Energy Association, global annual renewable capacity was nearly 510 gigawatts (GW) in 2023. As per Bloomberg New Energy Finance, developers deployed 444 GW of new photovoltaics (PV) capacity throughout the world in 2023. Driven by free fuel solar and wind as main energy sources and batteries for storing electric power, the transition to green energy on surface appears to be moving in the right direction. However, according to many published reports, world is not on track to meet net zero targets. The International Renewable Energy Agency (IRENA) says that world needs 1.1 TW of renewables per year so the world complies with targets set at the recent COP29 conference in the UAE. The bosses of the world’s leading oil and gas companies gathered recently at the industry’s annual Cera Week conference in Houston, Texas and claimed green energy transition is failing. Amin Nasser, chief executive of Saudi Aramco, the world’s largest oil company said, “We should abandon the fantasy of phasing out oil and gas, and instead invest in them adequately.”

articleTitle: Congratulations to 2023 PELS Awards Winners [Society News]
abstract: For nearly a century, the IEEE Awards program has paid tribute to technical professionals whose exceptional achievements and outstanding contributions have made a lasting impact on engineering, science, and technology. This tradition of public recognition continues today. In keeping with this tradition, IEEE Power Electronics Society (PELS) Awards Chair Andreas Lindemann of Universitaet Magdeburg, Germany announced the winners of IEEE PELS Awards, who were honored at a luncheon on 2 November at ECCE 2023 in Nashville, TN, USA. The ceremony was conducted by the awards chairs Fang Luo and Mahima Gupta and master of ceremonies Emmanuel Agamloh.

articleTitle: Digital Twins: The Real Opportunities [Industry Pulse]
abstract: Sometimes, knowing when a new buzzword has transitioned from hype to something real can be easy to identify. However, comprehending the opportunities beyond the hype can be more challenging, especially if several buzzwords are involved. NVIDIA’s GTC Conference keynote given by CEO Jensen Huang (viewed over 27 million times) <xref ref-type="bibr" rid="ref1" xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[1]</xref>, frequently mentioned “digital transformation” and its requisite enabler “Digital Twin,” in conjunction with artificial intelligence (AI). Hot topic conference talks, coupled with related investments and acquisitions, indicate that perhaps “Digital Twin” could be something real. In this edition of the Industry Pulse column, we will introduce you to the concept of the Digital Twin, how it differs from both AI and a traditional model, and examine the opportunities in power semiconductors and power electronic systems.

articleTitle: PELS SBC at NHCE India Organizes Distinguished Lecture
abstract: On 13 December 2023, IEEE Power Electronics Society (PELS) Student Branch Chapter (SBC) at the Department of Electrical and Electronics Engineering, New Horizon College of Engineering (NHCE), Bengaluru, India organized a Distinguished Lecture (DL) on “Solid-State Transformers: Journey from R&D to Recent Standard Development.” The DL lecture was organized from 10:00 am to 12:00 pm (local time) in association with IEEE PELS Bangalore Section Chapter (<xref ref-type="fig" rid="fig1" xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Figure 1</xref>). The PELS Distinguished Lecturer was Dr. Xu She, the director of electrical engineering, Lunar Energy, Mountain View, California, USA.

articleTitle: Petition for Nominations of PELS AdCom Members-at-Large
abstract: The Administrative Committee (AdCom) of the IEEE Power Electronics Society (PELS) is the top governance body responsible for governing and administering our Society, in the best interests of the IEEE, PELS members, and scientific and professional communities in the areas of the PELS field of interest. AdCom meets at least twice a year, deciding the strategic, governance, financial, and operational matters important to our Society (see details in the Power Electronics Society Bylaws, searchable online). A major part of PELS AdCom is the 18 members-at-large (MALs) elected by the members of the Society and representing over 13,000 PELS members worldwide. MALs are voting members of AdCom and are eligible for election candidates of the President-Elect, Vice Presidents and leaders of other committees of our Society. The term of each member-at-large is for three years starting from 1 January following the election in November of a year.

articleTitle: Patents: Prudent Investment With Future Potential or Inefficient Capital Allocation? [Patent Reviews]
abstract: One of the RAP sessions at the IEEE Applied Electronics Conference and Exposition (APEC) 2024, in Long Beach, CA, USA, debated the value of seeking patent protection for innovations and product improvements. This RAP session was a great success, sparking much debate and thoughtful discussion, if I do say so myself. I chaired the RAP session, and had an excellent panel to keep the discussion lively and interesting (many thanks to Grant Pitel, Patrick Chapman, Jeewika Ranaweera, and Prof. Johann W. Kolar for participating on the panel).

articleTitle: Remembering Prof. P. C. Sen: A Leader, Visionary, Educator, and a Mentor [In Memoriam]
abstract: Prof. Paresh Chandra (“P. C.”) Sen, professor emeritus in the Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering, Queen’s University at Kingston, Ontario, Canada, passed away in Kingston on 22 November 2023, at the age of 85 (<xref ref-type="fig" rid="fig1" xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Figure 1</xref>). Dr. Sen was born in 1938 in Chittagong, a city in present Bangladesh, where he grew up as an orphan, eventually moving to India to attend the University of Calcutta. He moved to Canada to pursue graduate study at the University of Toronto, where he earned his Ph.D. in 1967. He joined Queen’s University as a faculty member that year and made Kingston his home for the next 56 years. For all these years, he remained affiliated with the Queen’s university, building a reputation as a leader, visionary, educator, and mentor.

articleTitle: Report From Beijing [Industry Pulse]
abstract: <fig orientation="portrait" position="float" xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"> <graphic orientation="portrait" position="float" xlink:href="parri-3350308.tif"/> </fig> As a power electronics professional, but also a consumer, you are likely seeing frequent news stories about electric vehicles (EVs), and perhaps have driven or even own an electric car. In 2021, I purchased my first EV. But, it wasn’t a Tesla—300,000 cars sold in the U.S. in 2021 and 4 million sold globally that same year. It was a two-wheeled electric scooter, a mint-green Yadea which was one of 41 million sold just in China the same year. Today’s column is a bit of a departure from our regularly scheduled industry analysis, as I take a look on sustainability that’s niche where I’m from (the United States) but an everyday reality here in Beijing. Let’s take a look at this power electronics application that is a piece of the sustainable transport puzzle in many places, especially in IEEE Region 10 (Asian Pacific), and is only predicted to grow in popularity.

articleTitle: Buckapalooza—Part I [White Hot]
abstract: As an independent consultant I get requests to design custom ac–dc power supplies. Most often, the need is for a combination of output voltages and currents that are not available off-the-shelf. But, sometimes the need is for a specialized form factor. And at other times, the need is for a customized control or monitoring interface.

abstract: <fig orientation="portrait" position="float" xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"> <graphic orientation="portrait" position="float" xlink:href="butle-3350291.tif"/> </fig> The Power Electronics Society’s five-year strategic plan includes enhancing career support and development programs. This focus on career development was clearly seen at IEEE Energy Conversion Congress & Expo (ECCE) 2023 with its Women in Engineering (WIE) events program covering aspects from early career to senior leadership.

articleTitle: The 2023 Year-End Report and 2024 Preview [Students and Young Professionals Rendezvous]
abstract: <fig orientation="portrait" position="float" xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"> <graphic orientation="portrait" position="float" xlink:href="Kozak-3352219.tif"/> </fig> <fig orientation="portrait" position="float" xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"> <graphic orientation="portrait" position="float" xlink:href="Brand-3352219.tif"/> </fig> <fig orientation="portrait" position="float" xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"> <graphic orientation="portrait" position="float" xlink:href="Gehrk-3352219.tif"/> </fig> <fig orientation="portrait" position="float" xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"> <graphic orientation="portrait" position="float" xlink:href="Lin-3352219.tif"/> </fig>In the last calendar year, there were many changes within the organization, and it included a challenge to increase the purview of the Students and Young Professionals (S&YP) committee, as well as the events and services that the committee organizes and supports. This was done in part as nearly all major events returned to in-person attendance. To start, the S&YP committee expanded its normal suite of conference events by providing support to additional conferences as they began hosting new S&YP focused events. This support was offered to all conferences that IEEE Power Electronics Society (PELS) fully sponsors, with the hope to continue promoting networking, collaboration, and technical growth within the community.

articleTitle: IEEE PELS/IAS Joint Chapter at PPPEAC Takes Industrial Tour
abstract: On 8 September 2023, the IEEE Power Electronics Society (PELS)/Industry Applications Society (IAS) Joint Chapter at the Princeton-Philly Power Electronics Advancement Consortium (PPPEAC) was able to participate in an industrial tour of the Lockheed Martin facility in Moorestown, New Jersey, USA. The event included a tour of the facility, social event, and presentation about the history and accomplishments of the facility (<xref ref-type="fig" rid="fig1" xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Figure 1</xref>).

abstract: <fig orientation="portrait" position="float" xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"> <graphic orientation="portrait" position="float" xlink:href="lehma-3349992.tif"/> </fig> IEEE Power Electronics Society (PELS) is thrilled to share some groundbreaking developments that are shaping the trajectory of our community. articleTitle: New Elevated Engineer Series Introduces Emotional Intelligence (EQ) at APEC 2024 [Women in Engineering]
abstract: Elevating soft skills has just as powerful an impact on one’s career, if not more so, as improving technical skills. To help improve the soft skills of the Power Electronics Society (PELS) members, the PELS Women in Engineering (WIE) and Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI) committees introduced a new series called the Elevated Engineer with a breakfast event at this year’s IEEE Applied Power Electronics Conference and Exposition (APEC). The new Elevated Engineer series will bring professional development training to conference attendees who are looking to not only excel in their technical careers, but also grow their leadership and management skills.

articleTitle: YP Reception at APEC and Work Plan [Students and Young Professionals Rendezvous]
abstract: The IEEE Power Electronics Society (PELS) Students and Young Professionals (S&YP) Committee aims to provide resources and networking opportunities for students and young professionals. The committee supports and organizes many activities, such as conferences, webinars, workshops, and social receptions at large-scale international conferences. The most recent reception was held on 27 February, at the IEEE PELS Applied Power Electronics Conference and Exposition (APEC) in Long Beach, USA. The PELS S&YP Committee, along with the Industry Application Society (IAS) Young Professional Committee, supported the Power Sources Manufacturers Association (PSMA) lead YP reception with the slogan “Eat, Drink, and Talk With The Pros.” The YP reception was a fantastic opportunity for people from different places and backgrounds to meet and network, as shown in <xref ref-type="fig" rid="fig1" xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Figure 1</xref>. Over 100 attendees, including students, young professionals, and power electronics engineers and researchers participated in this event.

Principles of Power Electronics: Second Edition [Book Review]
abstract: While published as the second edition of “Principles of Power Electronics” the rewrites of the original text and additional new material warrant considering this as a new work in its own right. This is, as the authors say in the preface, a textbook and not a reference book. The authors in the Foreword offer different approaches to how this book could be used to teach different series of power electronics classes at the senior or graduate level. It is my take that this textbook is best when used as the basis for a full power electronics curriculum and not just to teach a one semester elective. The teaching approach aligns with my experience at MIT. This book teaches, as its title says, the principles of power electronics. This book does not teach a series of topologies or controls. Instead, the goal is for the student to develop a solid understanding of how we fundamentally process power using switch mode circuits and the tools and skills needed to understand how any power electronics circuit works. The book has 26 chapters and over 800 pages that are divided into four parts: Form and Function; Modeling and Control; Power Electronics Components and Devices, finally, and Practical Applications. This second edition of “Principles of Power Electronics” achieves the authors’ goal of creating a textbook to support a comprehensive curriculum in power electronics.

articleTitle: Jumping on the Accelerating Grid Train [Book Review]
abstract: In much of the world, photovoltaic (PV) power systems crossed a major threshold of “grid parity” by 2014, based on my personal experience with SolarBridge Technologies. When this happened, the operating-life value of energy produced by a complete PV plant installation dropped below the end customer electricity price. During 2017–2018, system costs had dropped below “cost parity,” when PV energy became competitive with coal and natural gas. At the time, one tagline of my presentations was “What happens when solar energy drops below grid parity and nobody notices?” Costs continue to drop. As this summary book by Divan and Sharma admirably documents, everybody notices now!
